newsitem.title: USA: US Postal Service taking mail off American.
newsitem.headline: US Postal Service taking mail off American.

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service began taking mail off American Airlines flights on Wednesday in anticipation of a potential strike by the airline's pilots union on Friday.

The Postal Service stopped putting mail on American Airlines flights originating in its Dallas-Ft. Worth hub, USPS national spokesman Roy Betts said. Mail will be put on other passenger airlines or will travel by truck instead.

American, a unit of AMR Corp., is the third-largest air carrier of U.S. mail, transporting 13.5 percent of parcels that are carried by plane. American transports 1.5 million pounds of U.S. mail each day, two-thirds of which goes through the main Southwestern postal center in Dallas, USPS Dallas spokesman Sam Bolen said.

About 200,000 pieces of mail originates in Dallas every day. The rest are processed and shipped out of the hub. The Postal Service is continuing to transport mail on American out of Chicago-O'Hare, San Francisco International Airport and JFK International in New York, Betts said.
Both Betts and Bolen said the Dallas stoppage will have minimal effects. The Postal Service is focusing on what to do should American shut down Friday night.

"We expect some minimal disruptions but we want to assure customers that the mail will keep moving and we are prepared to make the necessary adjustments in our operations to keep the mail moving," Betts said.
"The postal service is looking at extensive contingency plans," Betts said. He said mail will be transported by other airlines and by ground transportation including by truck and railroads.
Delta is the largest air mail carrier, transporting 18.6 percent of the mail that is transported by plane each year. United carries 18.3 percent.

The Postal Service has opened up its national command center in Washington to monitor the mail 24 hours a day. The command center has only been open around the clock before during the high-volume holiday season between Thanksgiving and New Year's.
Betts said it has not been determined how much money an American strike would cost the Postal Service.
American Airlines, which transports mail nationally and abroad for the Postal Service, did not immediately return a phone call.
The Allied Pilots Association says it will strike at midnight Friday if a settlement is not reached with American. The biggest issue is pay.
